item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
US envoy Steve Witkoff met President Putin in Russia after a positive meeting with President Zelenskyy, and during the talks Russia freed American Stephen Hubbard, who had been jailed for fighting for Ukraine. Ukraine conducted its first drone airlift of a wounded soldier from the front line, demonstrating a new evacuation capability. Russian forces continued strikes in Kyiv, killing four people, injuring two, and a separate drone attack wounded five people at a hospital. NATO increased patrol plane deployments in the Black Sea in response to the heightened Russian attacks. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli police detained ten settlers who attacked a photographer, a French mayor and other civilians, torched cars and olive trees, and wounded farmers in the West Bank. US politician Brad Lander and rabbis were briefly detained by Israeli forces during an olive harvest in the West Bank. UNICEF reports that 340 children have been killed in Gaza despite a ceasefire, while Gaza children face worsening food shortages as prices rise and aid is cut. A moderate settler group expressed support for what they described as "polite" ethnic cleansing. The conflict produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Houthis have stepped up missile and blast attacks in Yemen, killing 73 security recruits at a camp and striking a military camp in Aden, while also hitting a besieged city the UN says is at grave risk. In response, the United Kingdom is deploying Typhoon fighter jets and other air assets to protect Saudi Arabia from further Houthi strikes, and Saudi Arabia has postponed a major investment conference because of the attacks. The conflict caused 918 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Turkish forces continue to hold positions in Syria and Iraq, saying they will stay until border security is guaranteed, while armed groups have used explosive-laden drones to strike Syrian security posts in Suwayda. Israel is now backing Druze forces against President al-Sharaa, and Iranian Kurdish separatists have been deported to Iraq. Qatar’s intelligence chief says the country overhauled its entire defence system in six hours. DNA testing has identified seven family members killed in Syria, offering hope to the missing. UN-mediated peace efforts have resumed, aiming to end the drone war that is fueling the humanitarian crisis. The UN Security Council is holding a live session on the conflict’s spread, drones and the deadly impact of hunger. 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

In Ruweng fresh attacks left nine dead and six wounded, while bodies arrived from the Khor Kaltan killings in Northern Bahr el Ghazal. Communal clashes continued, including 14 deaths between Warrap and Lakes communities and the arrest of a traditional chief over a Juba youth killing. item.description:

The United States, through Secretary of State Marco Rubio, is urging Ethiopia and Eritrea to de-escalate, and Mekelle mayor Shishay Amare announced elections within six months to settle Western Tigray through constitutional processes. A drone strike in the disputed Abyei region killed at least 73 people, and the TPLF claims to have killed 1,511 Ethiopian soldiers in recent fighting.
